cleanStart.thinking: Off: CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL=unset and MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0, whatever effort the workspace or the provider declares.
cleanStart.environment: Built from nothing: the endpoint, token, model, custom headers and context window of the provider; PATH, locale, TMPDIR, certificates and proxies of the runner; ORBIT_HOME and the session context; nothing else of the runner's or the workspace's.

run.truncated: A run whose opening prompt reaches maxTurns ends with the CLI's error_max_turns: its turn is FAILED, and the runner reports it on the cursor route as outcome truncated, one more of the space's consecutive failures, with the cursor where it was. A plan job's run reported so ends its job failed instead (plan.jobs), and the cursor is neither moved nor counted.

cli.cursorAdvance: orbit wiki cursor advance --space <id> --to <token> [--outcome succeeded|failed|truncated] [--error TEXT] [--json]
cli.tool: none: maintenance verbs are CLI only, for a maintenance session, and have no MCP tool beside them.
cli.dossierPrecondition: Read dossiers only as a Wiki maintenance run of the space, and cite the records their lines name, never the dossier itself: a dossier is sessions compressed, redacted and cut to a budget, not a record.
cli.cursorPrecondition: Advance the cursor only when the run succeeded and every dossier up to the token was processed: a run that failed or was cut short reports that outcome instead, and moves nothing.

trigger.who: The server (WikiMaintenanceTrigger), for every space of the owner whose maintenance is on, when an event this replica published names a committed fact of the space that is still after the cursor: a session of the space at rest, an approval it answered, a merge receipt of it (all through the session's own events), or a settled task of the space (task.changed). A merge receipt or a criterion revision that publishes nothing of its own is counted in the backlog and taken in with the next fact that arrives.
trigger.conditions: Due when rules.backlogThreshold sessions have a fact after the cursor, or when the oldest fact after it is older than rules.maxPendingAgeHours as the new fact arrives. No clock starts a task: a space that turns due in silence makes its task with its next fact.
notMade: maintenance is off, or names no workspace or list
a task of the maintenance list has not ended (OPEN or IN_PROGRESS)
the event names no fact of the space after the cursor: a rename, the maintenance run's own events, another space's work
no fact past the settle grace is left to cover
held: the day's runs are used up, or a Manual space's review queue has no room
trigger.lock: The task is made under a lock on the maintenance list's row, after the list's unended tasks and the day's count are read again under it, so two facts arriving together make one task.

held.where: wiki_cursor.held_reason and held_at, served as the cursor state's held: {reason, at}, or null. Written when a due space makes no task for one of the reasons, keeping the time the reason first held; cleared when a task is made.
held.daily_limit_reached: The space has made settings.maintenance.dailyRunLimit maintenance tasks since midnight UTC (wikiMaintenanceRunsToday), however they ended.
held.review_queue_full: A Manual space, where every proposal waits for the owner, whose review queue has no room for one session's proposals.

job.runSize: How many sessions a run covers (wikiMaintenanceRunSessions), so that what it can propose fits its guardrails at rules.entriesPerSessionMax entries a session: in Manual, what one session may leave waiting (limits.opsPerSession) and what the review queue has room for; in Tiered and Automatic, reviewModes.rules.breakerMaxChangedPercent of the active entries when the space holds reviewModes.rules.breakerMinActiveEntries or more, and rules.runSessionsMax otherwise. Never more than rules.runSessionsMax.

task.list: the space's hidden Wiki maintenance list (maintenance.list)
task.title: Wiki maintenance: <space title>
task.provider: settings.maintenance.provider, pinned: the session is claimed as maintenance.run says
task.runAt: the moment it is made: the dispatcher's next scan starts it
task.creator: USER, the space's owner
task.description: the run's instructions: run `orbit wiki maintain --space <id>` once, and report what it printed
task.expect: The position a dossier page from the cursor would end at after the next runSize sessions, over the facts past the settle grace: the run pages from the same cursor up to it (the dossier route's until) and so reaches exactly it.

steps: context: GET …/maintenance/run — the space and its repository, the maintenance workspace's work directory, the topics, the guardrails' numbers and the position the task expects
checkout: the maintenance workspace's work directory, ~ expanded to the runner account's home, fetched; a checkout that is not the space's repository (its origin URL, its root commit) fails the run
dossiers: pages from the cursor up to the expected position (until); a dossier unchanged since it was processed is skipped

extract: one clean Claude Code call to the local model per dossier (the demo's A2+6: an 8k dossier, no thinking, at most rules.entriesPerSessionMax entries), told the space's repository and to answer {"offTopic": true} for a session about something else; each entry checked as the demo's extract.py checked it — kind, fields, each source a line of the dossier with its quote copied from that line, anchors that exist on origin/main — and the rejected ones asked for once more; a quote one of its line's spans holds (read as a quote is compared) is proposed as the record's own words there, with locator {start, end} (maintenance.job.citation), and one no span holds cites the record with neither

self-check: the entries as adds, grouped by topic into batches of at most limits.opsPerChangeset ops (limits.opsPerTurn in Manual), each proposed with dryRun; a quote the server does not find is dropped from its source and the op checked again, an op still refused is dropped, one the review queue holds back is not proposed, and one the breaker refuses is kept for the breaker step, which counts it with every other batch's

breaker: how many more entries the run may change through the mode is what the dry runs' breaker reading says (refusalRules.dryRun), the run's earlier changesets in the same session spent; from a server whose dry runs do not say, breakerMaxChangedPercent of the context's active entries when they are breakerMinActiveEntries or more. The pages are kept in the order read while what their ops would change fits; from the first page that does not fit, every op is held back (report ops.heldBackByBreaker) — a session on more than one page goes with the last of them — and the run's cursor stops at that page's from, so the next run reads those dossiers again. Nothing is recorded before this, and none of it fails the run
propose: each batch through POST …/maintenance/changesets, origin maintenance; an op the server refuses now fails the run

verify: in an Automatic space, orbit wiki verify's verification of the run's own ops, and one more pass for those left without a verdict; then the ops ended sessions left waiting (reviewModes.verification.adoption), at most rules.adoptOpsMax a run, the model set up for them when the run extracted nothing — one of them left without a verdict waits for the next run and fails nothing
anchors: orbit wiki anchors verify with --repo the checkout
articles: orbit wiki articles, which rewrites only the topics whose entry set changed
finish: POST …/maintenance/finish with the last page's token — or, when the breaker held ops back, the from of the first page it held back — outcome succeeded and the report
run.failure: A step that fails or a run cut short ends the run with outcome failed through the same finish route (truncated, through the cursor route, when the turn limit cut it): the cursor does not move, the space's consecutive failures go up by one, and the report says where it stopped. A breaker that holds ops back fails nothing: the run succeeds, and its cursor stops where the pages it held back start.
run.tokens: The report's tokens are every model call the run made — extraction, verification and articles — as Claude Code reported them.

job.offTopic: A session in the space's workspaces that is not about the space's repository yields no entry: the extraction prompt names the repository and what it is, and asks for {"offTopic": true} for such a session; and an entry whose code anchors none exist in the repository is dropped. Both are counted in the report (offTopic, entries.foreign).

citation.rule: A source an extracted entry cites is the record behind the line it names. Its quote, when the model gave one, is looked for in the words the line's spans hold, read as a quote is compared (backticks and asterisks aside, curly quotes straight, a run of whitespace one space): found in one span, the source carries the record's own words there — marks, quotes and spacing as the record has them, cut to limits.quoteMaxChars — as its quote, and where they are as its locator, code points of the record's redacted text. A quote no single span holds — the dossier's shorthand for the record, or words across a gap the dossier cut — and one holding words the redactor took out cite the record with no quote and no locator. A dossier from a server whose lines carry no spans keeps the line's words as the quote, and the self-check's dry run holds them to the record.
citation.strip: A quote the server does not find is taken off its source with its locator, and the op checked again (run.steps, self-check).

job.breaker: The circuit breaker over a run (wiki-maintenance-breaker.ts): a maintenance run's changeset counts reviewModes.floors.circuitBreaker over the whole run — every entry its earlier changesets changed through the mode is spent, those of an earlier attempt in the same session included, and the active entries are counted as they stood when the run began. A dry run answers with that reading (refusalRules.dryRun), and orbit wiki maintain holds its batches to it rather than counting anything of its own (run.steps, breaker).
job.report: What a run reports when it ends (WikiMaintenanceReport): sessions, dossiers, unchanged, offTopic, entries {extracted, kept, dropped, foreign, principles}, ops {proposed, recorded, refused, selfCheckDropped, heldBack, heldBackByBreaker, applied, waiting} (heldBack what the review queue's quotas held back, heldBackByBreaker what the run's breaker did), verification {verified, failed, and adopted {ops, verified, failed} when the run adopted any}, anchors, articles, tokens {input, output, calls}, seconds, and stoppedAt when it did not succeed. At most 16,000 bytes of JSON, kept on the run's row with ops.refused as a column of its own.

check.who: The space's owner's runner with no session — a task's acceptance command runs with none — or a maintenance run of the space; any other session WIKI_NOT_MAINTENANCE_SESSION, another owner's space a 404. It reads and writes nothing.
check.passes: The cursor at or past the expected position, and the latest run whose task expects that position ended succeeded with ops.refused 0.
check.exit: 0 when it passes; 1 otherwise, with each reason a sentence: the cursor before the position, no run expecting it, a run that did not say how it ended or did not succeed, a run that said nothing of its ops, or ops the server refused.

cli.tool: none: both are CLI only. maintain is a maintenance run's alone, and check is its task's acceptance command, which runs where there is no session.
cli.maintainPrecondition: Run this only as a Wiki maintenance run of the space, once, and let it finish: it proposes as the space's maintenance run, and it moves the cursor only when every step succeeded — a run that failed or was cut short moves nothing, and one whose breaker held ops back stops it where their dossiers start.
cli.checkPrecondition: Judge a maintenance run only by what this reads: it passes when the space's cursor reached the position the task expects and the server refused none of the run's ops, and a run cannot pass it by saying it finished.

health.who: The space's owner on the user door, as every read of the space: another account's space is the plain 404, and an account the wiki is not on for is answered WIKI_DISABLED. It writes nothing — not even the cursor row, which a space that never ran has none of yet.
health.entries: The space's active entries, every one of them: the status line's N entries. The entry list stops at limits of its own and is not a count.

maintenance.look: One of looks: what the status line draws.
maintenance.lastOkAt: When a run last succeeded (the cursor row's last_ok_at), or null.
maintenance.lastRunAt: When a run last reported how it ended, however it ended, or null.
maintenance.consecutiveFailures: Runs reported in a row that did not succeed; a succeeded run sets it back to 0 (maintenance.cursor.advance).
maintenance.backlog: The facts after the cursor (maintenance.cursor.backlog), counted from the facts as the read is made — the status line's N to catch up. Counted only while maintenance is on: a space that is off reads 0.
maintenance.oldestPendingAt: The oldest of those facts, or null; null too while maintenance is off.
maintenance.lagSeconds: How long ago that fact was, in whole seconds; 0 when there is none.
maintenance.dailyLimitReached: The space has made settings.maintenance.dailyRunLimit maintenance tasks since midnight UTC (wikiMaintenanceRunsToday), however they ended: no fact makes another today.
maintenance.held: maintenance.job.held as the cursor row keeps it: {reason, at}, or null.
maintenance.running: The run under way — its row has started and not ended, and its task is OPEN or IN_PROGRESS — as {sessionId, startedAt}, or null.
maintenance.lastRun: The run that ended last, as {sessionId, outcome, endedAt}, or null: what View run opens.

health.look: The first that holds, in the order of looks: off — maintenance is off; failing — consecutiveFailures is more than 0; running — running is not null; behind — the oldest fact after the cursor is older than maintenance.rules.maxPendingAgeHours; ok — none of those (wikiMaintenanceLook).

notify.push: PushService.notifyWikiMaintenanceFailing: one alert to the owner's devices, kind wiki-maintenance-failing, thread wiki-<space>, no badge — nothing is waiting for a reply.
notify.once: Sent by the one failure report whose increment made consecutive_failures exactly afterFailures. The increment is one UPDATE … RETURNING on the cursor row, so of reports racing only one reads that number back, and the streak's later failures read more. After the statement, outside any transaction, best-effort: the failure is recorded whether or not the phone rang.
notify.reset: A succeeded run sets consecutive_failures back to 0, so the next streak is told once more, at its own third failure.

health.client: The Wiki home's status line, on the web at every width and on iOS: after the entries, the review count (desktop only) and the anchors, the maintenance part in the space's look — the same words and the same parts on both, locked by src/shared/src/wiki-health.fixture.json.

articles.doc: docs/wiki-contract.md section 18; design section 3 wiki_topic_summary and section 12.1
articles.means: Each topic of a space has an article the local model wrote from the topic's active entries, every sentence footnoted to one of them; a topic with more entries than rules.splitAbove has an overview and subtopic articles instead. Articles are a view of the entries and a disposable cache (wiki_topic_summary): rewritten only when the topic's entry set changed, never pushed, never a source, and never returned by wiki_search or wiki_get.
articles.categoriesNote: The demo's six categories in the demo's order (平台核心, Runner 与引擎, 客户端与界面, 数据与后端, 工程流程, 协作), named in English as all UI copy is. wiki_topic.category is one of the keys, CHECKed; the directory lists the categories in this order.

kinds.article: part 0 of a topic that was not split: the topic's one article
kinds.overview: part 0 of a topic that was split: what the topic covers, pointing at its subtopic articles
kinds.subtopic: part 1 or later of a split topic: one group of its entries, hanging on the overview (parent_id)

articles.rulesNote: An article's length is counted in characters (Unicode code points) of its kept sentences, footnote markers and headings left out: the demo's measure, whose articles averaged 1,052 against a 400-900 target. The writer aims inside the range and asks again once when a draft falls short of minChars; the server cuts what passes maxChars (validation.cap). splitAbove, groupTarget, groupsMax and groupMin are the writer's grouping (the demo's), entriesPerArticle the most entries one article is written from.

membership.entries: A topic's entries are the space's active entries that no web-derived source tainted, each in exactly one topic.
order: paths: every repo-relative path the entry names (its path and symbol anchors, a pitfall's trigger.paths, a convention's scope up to its first wildcard) votes for the topic whose pattern claims the most of it (membership.patterns); the topic with the most votes wins, then the longer claim, then the earlier topic
declared: failing that, the first of the entry's own topics that is a topic of the space

text: failing that, the topic whose words its title, summary and aliases are closest to (tf-idf cosine over words and CJK bigrams against each topic's title, description and the entries the first two steps gave it); an entry close to none is in no topic
membership.why: The demo filed articles by the words alone, and a topic collected entries about something else (the sessions topic held articles on database writes and on running Nest). Where an entry is anchored in the code is the better witness, so it decides first.
membership.paths: A path is taken relative to the repository: a leading ./ and a checkout's absolute prefix (/root/orbit/, or a worktree's /.orbit/worktrees/<id>/) are dropped first.
membership.patterns: wiki_topic.path_prefixes holds prefixes and suffixes. A prefix claims a path that starts with it, as many characters as it has; one that ends in / claims the directory itself too (src/web claims what src/web/ does). A pattern that starts with * is a suffix: it claims a path that ends with the rest (*.swift claims a bare ConsoleModel.swift), as many characters as the rest has. So a directory's prefix outranks a suffix, and a suffix names what a bare file name is about when nothing longer does.

articles.fingerprint: sha256 of the lines <entry id>:<current revision> of the topic's entries, sorted by id and joined by a newline: the same entries at the same revisions give the same fingerprint, and an entry that joins, leaves or is amended changes it.
articles.regeneration: A topic's articles are rewritten only when its fingerprint differs from the one its part 0 was generated from, and only by a maintenance run after its entries changed (criterion 3): no clock starts one. A write that names the stored fingerprint rewrites nothing (unchanged), and one that names a fingerprint other than the topic's current one is refused WIKI_ARTICLE_STALE.

validation.input: Each part is Markdown with footnote markers [n], and notes: the entry each n names, notes[n-1]. A subtopic part names the entries of its group too.
validation.sentences: The body is cut into sentences at 。！？, and at a full stop or an ASCII ? or ! followed by a space or the end of the line — not at an ASCII ? or ! after a space or another ? or !, which is code left outside backticks (a ?? b, a != b), and not inside a code span; a heading line starts a block, and a first-level heading is not part of the body.
validation.markers: A marker survives only when n is 1 to the number of notes and notes[n-1] is an entry of the topic (a subtopic may cite any entry of its topic). A marker out of range, naming another topic's entry or naming no entry of the space is stripped.
validation.sentencesWithoutNotes: A sentence left with no marker is deleted.
validation.cap: When the kept sentences pass rules.maxChars, the last sentence of the longest block with more than one is dropped, again and again, until they do not.
validation.numbering: Footnotes are renumbered 1, 2, … in the order they first appear, and citations records the entry and its revision behind each number.
validation.empty: A subtopic part with no sentence left is dropped; a part 0 with none is not written at all, and the topic stays as it was.

view.push: Never in <orbit_wiki_context>: the push reads wiki_entry and nothing else.
view.source: Never a source: no source kind names an article (sourceRules.firstHand), so citing one is WIKI_SOURCE_UNRESOLVED.
view.agents: Never returned by wiki_search or wiki_get: both read entries alone, and an article's id is no entry's.
view.readers: The owner, on the user door. Another owner's space, topic or article is a plain 404.

who.write: A maintenance run of the space (isWikiMaintenanceSession, contract maintenance.session) through the runner door, and an import the API server's container runs itself (origin import, no session and no user) for a preview space. Every other caller is refused WIKI_NOT_MAINTENANCE_SESSION; the user door has no write route.
who.read: The owner, on the user door.

articles.seeding: A space with no topic yet is given articles.defaultTopics the first time a writer asks for its plan: their slugs, display names, categories, descriptions and path prefixes, in this order. A space that has topics keeps them.

reads.directory: The six categories in order, each with its topics (display name, description, the article's part 0 if there is one, and the subtopic parts under it), and the topics nothing has filed under a category.
reads.article: One part: its title, kind, blocks of sentences with their footnote numbers, and footnotes resolved to the entries they name (title, summary, kind, status, trust), with the topic, its category, the parts beside it, when and at which ref it was generated. It names every entry it was written from (entryIds, the pool its generation stored in wiki_topic_summary.entry_ids) and carries the first entriesListed of them as they stand now, the cited ones first (entries): what the list under the article is drawn from.
reads.index: Every article of the space, A to Z by title: its topic, its part and the entries it was written from.

articles.cleanClaudeCode: The verifier's clean launch (agentSurface.verify.cleanClaudeCode) with the writer's own system prompt, and thinking off: CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL=unset and MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0. The model reads entries only, never session text.

cli.tool: none: a maintenance run's verb, CLI only, with no MCP tool beside it.
cli.precondition: Write articles only as a Wiki maintenance run of the space, and only from what the model wrote: every sentence keeps a footnote to one of the topic's entries or is deleted, and a topic whose entries did not change is left as it is.
cli.does: Asks the plan for the topics whose entry set changed (--topic, one of them), reads each one's entries, groups a topic of more than rules.splitAbove entries into subtopics by their anchor paths and words, has the model name each group and write each article, and writes the topic's articles. It stops at the first 401 from the model's endpoint, and exits non-zero when any topic it took up was left unwritten.

plan.means: Before a space's documents are written, the local model drafts a plan: categories, the documents in each, every document's reader, scope, length and outline, and for every section the conditions its material is taken by. The server's gate checks each draft; the owner confirms one; documents are written only from the version the owner confirmed (guard). A plan is a record of what the owner agreed to, kept in versions, and not knowledge: it is never pushed, never a source, and never returned by wiki_search or wiki_get.

statuses.draft: stored after the gate passed it, waiting for the owner; a space has at most one, and a newer draft supersedes it
statuses.confirmed: the version the owner confirmed and the documents are written from; a space has at most one, and confirming a draft supersedes it
statuses.superseded: a version a newer draft or a confirmation replaced; kept, unchanged, as history

origins.maintenance: a whole draft a Wiki maintenance run's drafting job submitted through the runner door
origins.owner: the owner's edit of one document or section, or a proposal the owner accepted, through the user door

sectionKinds.overview: what the document covers, written last from what its other sections say
sectionKinds.concepts: a mechanism: what the things are; its material is the design documents, the code and the contracts
sectionKinds.flow: a mechanism: how it runs, step by step; its material is the design documents, the code and the contracts
sectionKinds.interface: a mechanism: the routes, tools, commands and their answers; its material is the contracts and the code
sectionKinds.data: a mechanism: the tables, fields and settings; its material is the migrations, the schema and the code
sectionKinds.ops: running it: deploying, operating, recovering; its material is the design documents and the scripts
sectionKinds.pitfalls: the known pitfalls; their material is what was said in sessions, found by the section's session condition
sectionKinds.decisions: the decisions and their reasons; their material is the owner's words and the records of decisions, found by the section's session condition
sectionKinds.conventions: the conventions to follow; their material is what was said in sessions, found by the section's session condition

plan.forAgents: A category with forAgents true holds the agents' development conventions (how to test, commit, land and run commands here): criterion 11 lists them as a category of their own, apart from the product and its mechanisms.
plan.rulesNote: docsMin and docsMax are the document count a draft is held to when its request names no target; a request may name its own (target: { min, max }, orbit wiki plan draft --target), up to docsCeiling. Lengths are counted in characters (Unicode code points). errorsMax is the most errors one refusal lists; its message counts them all.
plan.schemaNote: Every field a draft may carry, at each level, and no other. A draft's categories and docs are lists: a document names its category by key (a slug), and categories and documents are listed in the directory's order. A category needs key and title; a document every field but protected and extra, with audience, scopeIn and sections not empty; a section every field but key and extra. length is { min, max } for a document and one number for a section. A section's sources lists design-document sections ({ path, section }), code files with their symbols ({ path, symbols }) and contracts ({ path }); its session condition (sessions, or null) names projects (each by id or exact title), a time window (since and until, YYYY-MM-DD or null), keywords, anchor paths, entry kinds, topics (slugs of the space) and, in words, the original words to look for (evidence). A section's key is a slug, stable within its document from version to version: a section sent without one keeps the key its title had in the version revised, or is given the next s<n>.

newFields.rule: A field the schema does not have is refused at the gate, unless the draft declares it in newFields ({ at, name, why }) as a field that needs adding, at category, doc or section; then its values go in that object's extra, by name, apart from the schema's own fields, and the version's gate report lists it (needsNewFields) for the owner to read. A declared name that is already a field of the schema is refused, and so is a name in extra that newFields does not declare. An owner's edit and a proposal may use the fields the version they change declared, and declare none.

plan.versions: Every draft, edit and accepted proposal is a new version, numbered after every version the space has had and written in one transaction under the space row's lock (FOR NO KEY UPDATE); a version's documents and sections are only ever inserted, and the one row of a version ever updated is its own wiki_plan row, when it is confirmed or superseded. So a confirmed version never changes: what the owner confirmed is, byte for byte, what the documents are written from. Each version names the version it revises (baseVersion) and, for an accepted proposal, the proposal. A draft or an edit names the version it is built on (baseVersion; null for a space's first draft), which must be the space's newest version that is not superseded — its draft when it has one, else its confirmed version; one built on another is refused WIKI_PLAN_STALE and nothing is written. An acceptance is built on the newest version as it finds it, and is refused the same way when the plan moves while it is written.

gate.schema: Every field is one the schema has at its level (schema), or one declared as needing adding (newFields), of the right type and within rules; a section's kind is one of sectionKinds; category keys, document slugs and a document's section keys are unique.
gate.docCount: The plan has target.min to target.max documents: rules.docsMin to rules.docsMax unless the request names its own target.
gate.protected: A document the revised version protects is in the new version exactly as it was: the same slug, category and fields, and the same sections in the same order (their keys aside). Only the owner protects a document, so a draft or a proposal that protects one is refused. The owner's own edit is not checked: protecting is theirs.
gate.references: Every project a session condition names is one of the owner's (by id, or by an exact title only one project has), every topic a topic of the space, every entry kind one of the entry kinds; every document's category is one of the plan's categories, and every document a scope leaves something to (scopeOut[].docs) one of the plan's documents. A proposal's facts are an entry of the space or a session of the owner.
gate.repo: Files, docs sections, symbols and contracts exist only in a checkout, which the server has none of: the drafting job checks them on the runner at a commit and reports repoCheck { sha, checked, missing: [{ kind, ref, at }] } with the draft (kind one of file, docSection, symbol, contract). The server keeps the report and its sha beside the version (repo_sha, repo_check) and does not judge it; a version the owner made carries none.
gate.errors: A request the gate refuses is WIKI_PLAN_GATE with errors[]: everything it found, each { check, path, message }, the path from the request's root (a draft's plan.docs[3].sections[2].sources.sessions.projects[0], an edit's doc. or section., a proposal's change.doc.) — and for what an edit or a proposal would make of the whole plan, from that plan's (plan.docs[20].protected) — the first rules.errorsMax listed. Nothing is stored, so the drafting job hands the list to the model and asks again.
gate.report: A version the gate let through keeps its report: { checkedAt, checks (each passed, or skipped for protected on an owner's edit), docs, target, needsNewFields: [{ at, name, why, values }] }.

proposals.means: Knowledge a maintenance run found that fits no section of the confirmed plan is a proposed change to it: why (reason), the document as it should read — one of the plan's by its slug, or a new one, with the category it opens when it needs one the plan does not have (change: { doc, category }) — and the facts that led to it (facts: [{ kind, id }]). It is gated against the confirmed version, protection included, and stored pending. It changes no version until the owner accepts it.

statuses.accepted: the owner accepted it: its document was applied to the plan's newest version and made a new draft (resultVersion) for the owner to confirm
statuses.rejected: the owner rejected it; the plan is as it was

proposals.accept: Applies the document to the plan's newest version — in place of the document of its slug, or after the last document of its category — and gates the result again, protection included, since the plan may have moved since it was proposed: a result the gate refuses is WIKI_PLAN_GATE and the proposal stays pending. Otherwise the new draft and the proposal's settling are one transaction.
proposals.reject: Settles the proposal, with the owner's note if there is one; no version changes.

plan.guard: requireConfirmedPlan(db, { ownerId, spaceId }) in src/apiserver/src/wiki/wiki-plan.ts: the space's confirmed version ({ id, version, confirmedAt }), or WIKI_PLAN_UNCONFIRMED. Every writer of a space's documents calls it before it writes one, so no document is written from a plan the owner did not confirm; a maintenance run's proposal needs it too.

who.draft: A Wiki maintenance run of the space (isWikiMaintenanceSession, maintenance.session), through the runner door: its drafting job's draft, its read of the plan, and its proposals. Any other session is refused WIKI_NOT_MAINTENANCE_SESSION, a headless call 400, and another owner's space is a plain 404.
who.owner: The owner, through the user door and only there: every read of the plan, an edit, a confirmation, an acceptance or a rejection. A request with a session header is refused WIKI_OWNER_CHANNEL_ONLY before anything is read, whatever the session's role; the runner door has no route that confirms or decides anything. Another owner's space, version or proposal is a plain 404.

reads.state: { spaceId, confirmed, draft, proposals, job }: the version in force and the draft, each whole or null, the pending proposals, oldest first, and the space's plan job (plan.jobs.read), or null when it never had one.
reads.versions: Every version, newest first: { id, version, status, origin, baseVersion, proposalId, docCount, createdAt, confirmedAt, supersededAt }.
reads.version: One version whole: its status, origin, baseVersion, categories, newFields, target, gate report, repoCheck, model, who made and confirmed it and when, and its documents in order, each with its sections in order; a session condition's projects are { id, title } with the title as it stands now (null for a project since deleted).

requests.draft: { baseVersion, target?, plan: { categories, docs, newFields? }, repoCheck, model? }
requests.edit: { baseVersion, docSlug, doc } for a whole document (a new slug renames it), or { baseVersion, docSlug, sectionKey, section } for one of its sections
requests.propose: { reason, change: { doc, category? }, facts: [{ kind, id }] }
requests.redraft: { instructions? }: with instructions (at most plan.jobs.rules.instructionsMaxChars characters) a revision, without them a draft

plan.view: Not knowledge: no source kind names a plan, so citing one is WIKI_SOURCE_UNRESOLVED; the push and the agent's search and get read entries alone.
plan.tool: none: no MCP tool reads, confirms or decides anything of the plan (hard constraint 2). The drafting job's verbs are the CLI's.

jobs.means: A space's plan is drafted, revised and built by jobs the server runs as tasks of the space's hidden Wiki maintenance list (maintenance.list), so the session that runs one is a maintenance session (isWikiMaintenanceSession) and the plan's runner door is open to it and to nothing else. A fact asks for a job — the space's creation, or its owner — never a clock.

kinds.draft: orbit wiki plan draft: a whole plan drafted from the repository at origin/main and what the space already knows, keeping every document the version it revises protects
kinds.revise: orbit wiki plan revise: the space's newest version revised with the owner's instructions; a space with no version yet is drafted with the instructions as the owner's guidance
kinds.build: the documents written from a confirmed version: kept for the task that writes them, which makes its own jobs

triggers.space_created: the space was created: through POST /api/wiki/spaces, or on the first proposal of a session whose workspace's repository had no space yet
triggers.owner: the owner asked on the plan page: POST /api/wiki/spaces/:id/plan/redraft

states.queued: the space's maintenance list has a task that has not ended; the job is made when a task of the owner's ends
states.held: the space's maintenance names no workspace, or a provider no run could start on (held.reason); the job is made when the owner's next change to the maintenance settings, or their next request, finds that settled
states.running: its task is made: dispatched, or running, with the gate round it is on
states.succeeded: its run stored a draft the gate let through (version)
states.failed: its run ended without one — errors are the gate's on its last round — or its task ended before the run said how it went

held.where: wiki_plan_job.held_reason and held_at, served as the job's held: { reason, at }, or null. Written when a job is not made for one of the reasons, keeping the time the reason first held, as maintenance.job.held is on the cursor; cleared when its task is made.
held.no_maintenance_workspace: settings.maintenance.workspaceId names no workspace of the owner's: a draft runs where maintenance runs.
held.maintenance_provider_unusable: settings.maintenance.provider is one no maintenance run could start on (wikiMaintenanceProviderProblem): missing, turned off, or not on the Claude Code runtime.

jobs.request: A request asks for a draft, or with instructions a revision. The space's draft or revision that has not ended answers it (one open a space, a partial unique index) and is asked again whether it may be made now; a made job whose task already ended, or is gone, without its run saying how is ended failed first, so it cannot stand in the way. Otherwise a job is recorded and asked at once: held when the settings say so; queued when the list has a task that has not ended; else made.
jobs.trigger: WikiPlanJobFacts takes every task change this replica publishes (task.changed): the made jobs of the tasks it names are ended failed when their task ended before the run said how it went, and the owner's queued jobs are asked again, since the list may have just been freed. The owner's change to a space's maintenance settings asks its queued and held jobs again. No clock asks anything.
jobs.staggered: A job and the space's maintenance runs share its list, one task at a time: the maintenance trigger makes no task while the list has one that has not ended (maintenance.job.trigger.notMade), and a job waits behind one the same way, so the local model is never asked by both at once.
jobs.notAMaintenanceRun: A job's task is not a maintenance run: it is not counted against settings.maintenance.dailyRunLimit (wikiMaintenanceRunsToday counts the list's other tasks), the day's limit does not hold it back, and it runs whether or not maintenance is turned on — the list is made for it when the space has none, and the claim does not refuse its session for maintenance being off (maintenance.run).

task.list: the space's hidden Wiki maintenance list (maintenance.list), made for the job when the space has none
task.title: Wiki plan draft: <space title>, or Wiki plan redraft: <space title> for a revision
task.provider: settings.maintenance.provider, pinned: the session is claimed as maintenance.run says
task.runAt: the moment it is made: the dispatcher's next scan starts it
task.creator: USER, the space's owner
task.description: the run's instructions: run `orbit wiki plan draft --space <id>` (or `revise`) once, and report the documents, the gate rounds with their errors, the token spend and the time it printed; a revision's instructions are quoted below them

jobs.read: The plan's read (plan.reads.state) carries the space's job that has not ended, else the one that ended last: { id, spaceId, kind, trigger, state, instructions, requestedAt, held, waitingFor: { taskId, title, sessionId, startedAt } for a queued one, taskId, provider, sessionId, madeAt, startedAt, endedAt, attempt, attemptsMax, version, errors, error, report, draft } — draft being the last draft of a failed job, as its run sent it to the gate.

who.redraft: The owner, on the owner channel only: a request with a session header is refused WIKI_OWNER_CHANNEL_ONLY before anything is read. Its answer is { created, job }: the job made, or the space's draft that had not ended.
who.runner: context, progress, finish and materials are a maintenance run's of the space alone, as the plan's other runner routes are: any other session WIKI_NOT_MAINTENANCE_SESSION, a headless call 400, another owner's space a plain 404. context, progress and finish answer a maintenance run whose task no job was made for WIKI_PLAN_NO_JOB, and progress a job that has ended the same way, as finish does any end but the one the job ended with. check answers the space's owner's runner with no session too — a task's acceptance command runs with none.

jobs.context: { job, space: { id, title, repo: { urlNorm, rootCommitSha }, workspace: { id, workDir } } }: the job the calling session's task was made for and where its run starts; records the session and the time it first started.
jobs.progress: { attempt }: the gate round the run is on, 1 to rules.attemptsMax — what the plan page shows while it runs.
jobs.finish: { outcome: succeeded | failed, version?, errors?, error?, report?, draft?, attempt? }: a run that succeeded names the version its draft became, a draft of the space this very session stored; one that failed carries the gate's errors on its last round (at most plan.rules.errorsMax), what went wrong in words (redacted, at most rules.errorMaxChars), and the last draft it had (at most rules.draftMaxBytes of JSON). The report is at most rules.reportMaxBytes of JSON. The job is ended with it, once: the same end said again by the run that said it (the runner sends it again when the answer to its first send was lost) is answered with what was kept and changes nothing; any other end is refused WIKI_PLAN_NO_JOB.

check.passes: The job ended succeeded, and the version it names is one of the space's.
check.exit: 0 when it passes; 1 otherwise, with each reason a sentence: the run did not say how it ended, it failed (with its error and how many errors the gate's last round found), or the version it names is missing.

jobs.materials: { spaceId, title, asOf, repo, workspace, projects: [{ id, title, status, createdAt, tasks, sessions }], sessions: { days, total, items: [{ title, month, task, project, provider }] }, entries: [{ kind, status, count }], topics: [{ slug, title, category, pathPrefixes, active, recent: [{ kind, title }] }] }: the owner's projects (at most rules.materialsProjectsMax, oldest first), the sessions of the space's workspaces of the last rules.materialsSessionDays days (at most rules.materialsSessionsMax, newest first, with the total), and how the space's entries and topics are spread. Every title is redacted before it leaves the server; the runner counts and clusters.
jobs.report: What a run reports when it ends (WikiPlanJobReport): categories, docs, sections, target, attempts [{ attempt, local, server, checks }] — each gate round's errors found by the runner's own gate and by the server's, by check — repo { sha, checked, missing }, tokens { input, output, calls }, seconds, model, and rulesDraft: the fourth step's draft of the rules, cut to fit.

steps: context: GET …/plan/job — the job, the space, its repository and the maintenance workspace's checkout; and GET …/plan — the version it revises and the documents that version protects
checkout: the maintenance workspace's work directory, ~ expanded to the runner account's home, fetched; a checkout that is not the space's repository fails the run

materials: the repository at origin/main — its modules and entry points, the docs heading tree (docs/mocks and docs/evidence left out), the contracts and the code's symbols — and GET …/plan/materials, the owner's projects, the space's sessions counted and clustered by title, and its entries and topics

draft, in four steps each streamed to disk as it is written: the catalogue's skeleton (categories and documents), each category's documents in detail, each document's outline with where every section's material comes from, and a draft of the rules; one clean Claude Code call to the local model a unit, in a compact line format

gate: the runner's own gate first — schema, docCount, protected, references (files, docs sections, symbols and contracts at the sha, every project and topic, and every → x.y or 见 x.y a document of the plan) and, for a revision, sections moved out only of kind conventions — then the server's (POST …/plan/drafts)
redo: whatever either gate found is handed back to the model, unit by unit, and the draft gated again: rules.attemptsMax rounds in all
finish: POST …/plan/job/finish with the version the draft became, or the last round's errors
run.revise: A revision asks the model for the new catalogue — each document with the documents of the version it revises that it is made from, and the sections it moves into a category for agents — then writes again only the documents that merge or are new; one made from a single document of the version keeps its outline, less the sections moved out. A protected document is carried as it is, and a move out of one, or of a section of any kind but conventions, is refused by the runner's gate.
run.model: Every call is a clean Claude Code (agentSurface.verify.cleanClaudeCode) on the model this session's provider names, thinking off, its answer streamed to a file as it arrives; the run waits for the endpoint's /health before its first call and stops at the first 401.

cli.draft: orbit wiki plan draft --space <id> [--target MIN-MAX] [--model MODEL] [--concurrency N] [--work-dir DIR] [--json]
cli.revise: orbit wiki plan revise --space <id> [--instructions <file>] [--target MIN-MAX] [--model MODEL] [--concurrency N] [--work-dir DIR] [--json]
cli.tool: none: all three are CLI only. draft and revise are the plan job's run alone, and check is its task's acceptance command, which runs where there is no session.
cli.draftPrecondition: Run this only as the plan job of the space, once, and let it finish: it drafts as the space's maintenance run, and only a draft that passed the plan's gate is stored — three rounds at most, each handing every error back to the model.
cli.revisePrecondition: Run this only as the plan job the owner's redraft made, once, and let it finish: it revises the plan's newest version with the owner's instructions, and only a draft that passed the plan's gate is stored — three rounds at most, each handing every error back to the model.
cli.checkPrecondition: Judge a plan job only by what this reads: it passes when the job's run stored a draft that passed the plan's gate, and a run cannot pass it by saying it finished.

docs.means: A space's documents, written section by section from the plan its owner confirmed (plan.guard): a document is a plan document, named by its slug, and a section a plan section, named by its key. Every footnote points at a first-hand original — a design-document section, code or a contract at a commit, or one of Orbit's own records — with its verbatim quote, and the entry it was found through is kept as the via entry: an entry is the way in, never the source. What each sentence is, and how each footnote was checked, is stored sentence by sentence. A document is a view for people: never pushed, never a source, and never returned by wiki_search or wiki_get. The topic articles (articles, wiki_topic_summary) stay, readable as they are, until the clients have moved to the documents.

statuses.ok: no more than rules.needsReviewAbove of its sentences are unsourced or unverified
statuses.needs_review: more than rules.needsReviewAbove of its sentences are unsourced or unverified: the whole document is marked for review

sentenceStatuses.sourced: it carries a footnote whose check passed (verdict verified)
sentenceStatuses.transition: it carries no footnote and brings no new fact: every fact token in it (factTokens) is already in a sourced sentence or a heading of the same document
sentenceStatuses.unsourced: it carries no footnote and states a fact no sourced sentence or heading of the document carries; the tokens that are new are stored with it
sentenceStatuses.unverified: it carries footnotes, and none of them passed its check
sentenceStatuses.withdrawn: a footnote of it came through an entry since rejected, retired or superseded, or whose anchor changed or went missing (withdrawal); it stays, struck through, until its section is written again

footnoteKinds.design_doc: a section of a design document in the repository: path@sha#Lstart-end, and the section's heading
footnoteKinds.code: code in the repository: path@sha#Lstart-end, and the symbol
footnoteKinds.contract: a contract in the repository: path@sha#Lstart-end
footnoteKinds.turn: a conversation turn, by its id
footnoteKinds.event: a run event — a reply, a thinking, a tool call's input or its result, an error — by its id
footnoteKinds.tool_call: a tool call's output, by its id
footnoteKinds.task: a task's title and description, by its id
footnoteKinds.task_comment: a task comment, by its id
footnoteKinds.approval: an approval's answers and note, by its id
footnoteKinds.owner_decision: a blocker the owner resolved with a note, by its id
footnoteKinds.merge_receipt: a merge receipt, by its id
footnoteKinds.note: a file orbit wiki import registered, by its id

verdicts.verified: the quote is in the original
verdicts.not_found: the quote is not in the original; a quote shorter than rules.quoteMinChars once folded is not checked, and is not found either
verdicts.no_quote: the footnote gave no quote, so nothing could be checked
verdicts.unresolved: the record it names is not one of this account's — another owner's, deleted, or none at all; a repository footnote is never unresolved

checkers.server: a record's footnote: the server read the record again and checked the quote itself
checkers.runner: a repository footnote: the runner checked the quote at sha, in the checkout the server does not have

blockKinds.item: a list item, cut into sentences
blockKinds.heading: a heading inside the section: its text, which counts as a heading for factTokens
blockKinds.code: a fenced code block: its text, which is not checked

docs.rulesNote: Lengths are counted in characters (Unicode code points). needsReviewAbove is a share of all the document's sentences, withdrawn ones included: more than it marks the whole document, and exactly 5% does not. quoteMinChars counts the folded quote (verification.normalization). sectionsPerWrite is plan.rules.sectionsMax, so one write can carry a whole document. errorsMax is the most errors one refusal lists; its message counts them all.
docs.schemaNote: Every field a write may carry, at each level, and no other: anything else is refused WIKI_DOC_INVALID. planVersion, repoSha (the origin/main commit the run read the repository at, 40 lowercase hex) and sections are required; model is not. A section needs key (a section of the confirmed plan's document, once per write), materialSha256 (64 lowercase hex), markdown (not blank, at most rules.markdownMaxChars) and footnotes (at most rules.footnotesPerSection, and may be empty). A repository footnote (repoKinds) needs path, sha (7-64 lowercase hex: one with no sha is refused), lines { start, end } (1-based, inclusive) and verified, the runner's own check; section, symbol, quote, excerpt and viaEntryId are optional. A record footnote (recordKinds) needs ref, the record's id; chars { start, end } (code points of the record's redacted text, end exclusive), quote and viaEntryId are optional. viaEntryId, when given, is an entry of the space. A quote is at most rules.quoteMaxChars; null or left out is no quote.
docs.markdown: A section's body is Markdown with footnote markers [n], n naming its section's footnotes[n-1]. A first line that is a heading is the section's own title, which the plan names, and is dropped. A fenced code block is one code block and is not checked; any other heading line is a heading block; a list item (-, *, +, 1., 1), 1、) is an item block, and an indented line under it continues it; other lines up to a blank line are one paragraph (a leading > is dropped, a line of three dashes, stars or underscores is skipped). Paragraphs and items are cut into sentences as articles.validation.sentences cuts an article — at 。！？, and at a full stop or an ASCII ? or ! before a space or the line's end, outside code spans — so a ； ends nothing. A marker outside a code span names a footnote; one outside 1 to the section's footnote count names none and is dropped (stats.markersDropped), and a run of markers with no words is not a sentence. A section with no sentence is refused.

verification.records: The server reads the record again, among the account's own rows, through the one reader a record has (WikiService.sourceText, whose texts wiki-verify-evidence.ts defines: runEventText for an event, a tool call's name, input and output together, an approval's answers and note — and the plan it decided — a merge receipt's and an owner decision's line as the dossier writes them), so a document and an entry citing the same record check their quotes against the same words; it redacts it with the shared redactor and the owner's workspace.env values, and looks for the quote — redacted the same way — in it, both folded (normalization). chars, when given, narrows the search to that range. The range the quote was found at is stored (char_start, char_end: code points of the redacted text), and so are the record's session, number, time and label, for the page's link. A translated, paraphrased or spliced quote — two passages of the record joined as one — is not found.
verification.repository: The server has no checkout. A repository footnote carries the runner's own check of its quote against the lines it names (verified) and the commit it read them at (sha); it is stored as checked by the runner at that sha, and a footnote with no sha is refused. excerpt, when the runner sends it, is those lines as it read them, redacted, for the page to show.
verification.normalization: Before a quote is compared, quote and original alike are folded: Unicode NFC; the full-width punctuation ，。：；（）！？「」“”‘’、『』【】—– read as its ASCII counterpart; ** and __ and backticks dropped; a Markdown escape read as the character it escapes; every whitespace dropped. The original is compared a second time with each line's leading comment marker (//, ///, /*, *, */ or #) taken off, so a quote of a comment's words is found. A quote is one passage: an ellipsis is not a gap to skip.

docs.factTokens: A sentence's fact tokens: each code span (its content); each ASCII identifier or path ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_./-]*[A-Za-z0-9_]) of at least 3 characters that is not one of the, and, for, with, not, are, can, its, but, via; each number of two or more digits; and each number with a unit (秒 分钟 小时 天 个 条 次 % ms s MB KB) — matched in that order, lowercased, whitespace dropped.
docs.classification: A sentence with a footnote is sourced when one of its footnotes is verified and unverified when none is; withdrawn when one of them came through an entry withdrawal names. A sentence with none is a transition when every fact token in it is among those of the document's sourced sentences and headings — its plan sections' titles, the heading blocks of its written sections, its title and its question — and unsourced otherwise, its new tokens stored with it. The whole document is classified again each time a section of it is written, so a transition answers to what the other sections say now. The document is needs_review when its unsourced and unverified sentences are more than rules.needsReviewAbove of all of them; withdrawn sentences are not counted among those: they wait for their section to be written again.
docs.fingerprint: materialSha256 is the runner's: sha256 over the section's definition in the plan (title, kind, covers, length, sources) and the material it gathered for it, as it gathered it. The server does not recompute it; it compares it with the one stored.
docs.repoSha: Every section is stored with the origin/main commit it was generated at (repoSha, from the write that wrote it), and a document with its last write's. A maintenance run compares a section's repoSha with origin/main as it stands, and writes again a section whose design documents, code or contracts changed since (owner 2026-09-29: the wiki follows what agents write into docs/); that comparison is the run's, and the server only keeps the sha and hands it back (reads.writerState, reads.doc).
docs.regeneration: A section whose stored materialSha256 is the one a write names, and from which nothing was withdrawn (stale_at null), is not written again: its outcome is unchanged and its rows are left as they are. Every other section a write names is replaced whole, its sentences and footnotes with it. A write names the confirmed plan version it was written from (planVersion); one that is not the confirmed version is WIKI_PLAN_STALE and writes nothing. A section the confirmed plan's document no longer has is dropped when the document is next written. No clock rewrites anything (hard constraint 5): the maintenance run writes after facts arrived.
docs.withdrawal: When an entry is rejected, retired or superseded, or its anchor state becomes changed or missing, every sentence with a footnote that came through it (via entry) is withdrawn — status withdrawn, with when, why (withdrawReasons) and the entry — and its section is marked stale (stale_at), so the next maintenance run writes it again. It happens in the entry's own transaction, at its single state writer (WikiService.recomputeFlags, which every applyOp branch ends in; storage.singleWriter), so no path that moves an entry can forget it. A write with a footnote that comes through such an entry stores that sentence withdrawn, and its section stale, at once; and it takes its via entries FOR SHARE before anything else, so a rejection racing it waits for it and then withdraws what it wrote.

links.sessionRecord: A footnote on a turn, an event or a tool call carries the record's id (recordId) and the session it is in (sessionId), both read when the write checked it: wiki_source keeps a record's id alone, and the page needs the pair to link the record — web sessionRecordHref(sessionId, recordId), iOS SessionRecordLink.url(session:record:), which open the session at it through GET /api/sessions/:id/events/page?around=<recordId>. Any other record carries what it is in: an approval or a merge receipt its session (sessionId), a task comment its task (taskId), an owner decision its project (projectId), a note its path (notePath).
links.repository: A repository footnote carries its path, sha and lines (path@sha#Lstart-end): the page links that file at that commit in the space's repository.

view.push: Never in <orbit_wiki_context>: the push reads wiki_entry and nothing else.
view.source: Never a source: no source kind names a document, a section, a sentence or a footnote (sourceRules.firstHand), so citing one is WIKI_SOURCE_UNRESOLVED.
view.agents: Never returned by wiki_search or wiki_get: both read entries alone, and a document's ids are no entry's.
view.readers: The owner, on the user door. Another owner's space or document is a plain 404.

who.write: A maintenance run of the space (isWikiMaintenanceSession, maintenance.session) through the runner door, and an import the API server's container runs itself (origin import, no session and no user). Every other caller is refused WIKI_NOT_MAINTENANCE_SESSION, a headless call 400, another owner's space a plain 404; the user door has no write route. Every write asks requireConfirmedPlan first (plan.guard): with no confirmed plan it is WIKI_PLAN_UNCONFIRMED.
who.read: The owner, on the user door.

reads.directory: { spaceId, plan: { version, confirmedAt } | null, docs: { total, written }, categories }: the confirmed plan's categories in its order (number from 1), each with its documents (number <category>.<n>, title, question, written, status, updatedAt, planVersion) and each document's sections (number, title, kind, written, stale). A space with no confirmed plan has none.
reads.doc: One document of the confirmed plan: its number, title, question, audience, scope (scopeOut's documents with their number and title), category, length, status, and when, from which plan version and at which origin/main commit (repoSha) it was written; its sections in the plan's order, each with the commit it was generated at and its blocks, a block's sentences each with its status, its footnote numbers, its new tokens and, once withdrawn, why, when and through which entry; its footnotes, numbered by first appearance — the same original and quote cited twice is one number — each with its kind, verdict, who checked it, its quote, its location (path@sha#Lstart-end, or <kind>:<record id>#c<start>-<end>) and what the page links to (links): a repository original's path, sha, lines, section, symbol and excerpt; a record's id (recordId), character range, session (sessionId, with recordId the pair a turn's, an event's or a tool call's deep link needs) and its title, number, time and label, task and project and their titles, a note's path; and its via entry; and the via entries as they stand now, with the footnotes each carried. A document of the plan not written yet is written false with its sections unwritten; one the plan does not have is a 404. counts and unsourcedShare are its sentences' as they stand.
reads.index: Every document of the confirmed plan, and every section whose title no other document of the plan shares — the ones every document has (known pitfalls, conventions, overview) are left out — each with its document's number and title, its category and whether it is written, in title order.
reads.writerState: { spaceId, planVersion, docs: [{ slug, planVersion, status, repoSha, updatedAt, sections: [{ key, materialSha256, repoSha, stale, generatedAt }] }] }: what is written, for a run to tell which sections to write again — a stale one, one whose material changed, or one whose repoSha origin/main has moved past in what it cites.

requests.write: { planVersion, repoSha, model?, sections: [{ key, materialSha256, markdown, footnotes: [{ kind, path, sha, lines, section?, symbol?, quote?, excerpt?, verified, viaEntryId? } | { kind, ref, chars?, quote?, viaEntryId? }] }] }

docs.tool: none: no MCP tool reads or writes a document. Writing is a maintenance run's verb on the CLI; reading is the owner's, in the Wiki.

refusals.when: The wiki is off for this account (ORBIT_WIKI rollout).
The calling session's workspace is bound to no space and could not be bound on first use. The message says in one sentence how the owner binds it.

The op, its entry, its anchors or its sources do not have the shape this contract gives them: a kind's fields (KIND_SPECS), a limit, a phase-3 kind, an amend of a decision, a baseRevision where one is required or forbidden. errors[] names every field that failed.
A non-owner op adds, amends or supersedes a kind only the owner writes (kinds.<kind>.ownerOnlyOps).
A source does not resolve among the owner's own rows, cites a wiki entry or view, or an op that must cite a source cites none.
A quote, whitespace-normalized, is not a substring of the text of the record it cites.
An amend, supersede or retire names a baseRevision that is not the entry's current revision. The answer carries the current revision and a diff.

The op is past limits.opsPerChangeset in its request; or it would wait for the owner and pass limits.opsPerTurn for the request or limits.opsPerSession for the calling session (limitNotes.quota); or the review mode would apply it and the changeset would pass the circuit breaker (reviewModes.floors).
The op would wait for review and the space already has limits.pendingOpsPerSpace pending ops that wait on the owner's decision (spot checks and ops waiting for their verification not counted).
The title or text reads as a tool probe (test, probe, TEST_WRITE_CHECK). The message says the tool works and not to retry.

A decide, a revert, an entry's Reject or Confirm, a reopening of verifications, a change of the review mode or of automaticSpotChecks, or any request of the plan's on the user door (plan.who.owner) arrived with a session header, whatever the session's role: each is the owner's, on the user door, with no acting session.
A maintenance-only route was called by a session that is not a maintenance run of that space.
The calling session verifies, forems or judges work (task.verifiesTaskId, task.isForeman, a judgment session). Knowledge is not evidence, so such a session neither reads nor proposes.
An idempotency key the owner already used arrived with a different request (its normalized digest differs). The same request under the same key is a replay and gets the recorded answer.

A succeeded run asked to advance the cursor to a token behind the space's watermark: another run already went further, and the cursor only moves forward (maintenance.cursor.advance). The answer carries the cursor as it stands.
A cursor token that no dossier page of this space handed out: one that does not decode, one of another space, or a position past the furthest page the space's dossier route has issued.

An article write named an entry-set fingerprint that is not its topic's current one: the topic's entries changed while the articles were being written (articles.regeneration). Nothing is written; the next run writes them from the entries as they stand.

A plan draft, an owner's edit of the plan, a proposed change to it or the acceptance of one did not pass the plan's gate (plan.gate): errors[] lists everything it found, each with its check and where it is. Nothing is stored.

A plan request was built on a version that is no longer the space's newest (plan.versions), confirmed a version that is no longer a draft, or answered a proposal already decided. Nothing is written; read the plan again.
A space's documents were to be written, or a change proposed to its plan, and the space has no plan its owner confirmed (plan.guard).

A maintenance run asked for, or reported on, a job of the space's plan, and its task was made for none, or the job has ended — its run said how, or its task ended first (plan.jobs.who.runner). Nothing is written.

A document write does not have the shape docs.schema gives it: a field it does not name, a repository footnote with no sha or no lines, a record footnote with no id, a section the confirmed plan's document does not have, a via entry that is not an entry of the space. errors[] lists everything it found, each { path, message }, the first docs.rules.errorsMax. Nothing is written.

refusalRules.orderNote: The order each op is checked in (design section 4.1); redaction, taint, effect and similar refuse nothing, they mark the op. changesetSize is limits.opsPerChangeset, read off the op's position alone. quota comes after the effect because what it counts depends on it: the review queue, the ops that wait (limitNotes.quota), and the circuit breaker, which counts what the review mode applies.
refusalRules.perOp: Each op is judged on its own. The ops that pass are recorded in one transaction; a refused op writes nothing.
refusalRules.status: A request none of whose ops was recorded answers with the HTTP status of its first refusal and every op's outcome in the body. A request that recorded something answers 200.
refusalRules.dryRun: Checks every op and answers as the request would, recording nothing and publishing nothing. Its answer also carries breaker: the circuit breaker as the request found it, before any of its ops — {scope, activeAtStart, changed, remaining}: scope run for a maintenance run's changeset (maintenance.job.breaker) and changeset otherwise, activeAtStart the active entries it is counted against, changed the entries already changed through the review mode, and remaining how many more distinct entries the mode may change before an op is refused, null where no op is held to the breaker (a Manual space, the owner's own write, a space holding fewer than reviewModes.rules.breakerMinActiveEntries active entries). A request of the same ops recorded now refuses exactly the ones past remaining.
refusalRules.idempotency: An idempotency key is the owner's: the same key with the same normalized request returns the recorded answer, marked replayed, and writes and publishes nothing.
refusalRules.notFound: Another owner's space, entry or changeset is a plain 404 with no wiki code, the same answer as one that does not exist.
refusalRules.serviceToken: A service token is refused on both doors (403), as session_search refuses it: entries derive from conversation text on other machines.

agentSurface.why: An agent reads the wiki and proposes to it; it never decides. Three tools, split by risk rather than by entity.

wiki_search.returns: entries only: id, kind, title, summary, trust, anchorState, match (searchMatches) and score

wiki_get.returns: whole entries; each anchor with its last check (the ref and the time); each source with its orbit-* link

wiki_propose.returns: per op: pending (with waitsFor verification when an automatic space's verification, not the owner, decides it), applied, conflict (current revision and diff) or refused (reasons); similar[] beside an add or supersede

agentSurface.notTools: No tool accepts, confirms, decides, hard-deletes or overwrites a page. Confirmation exists only on the owner channel.
agentSurface.proposeDescription: Record only what someone could not read from the code: a decision and what was rejected, a pitfall and its fix, a convention. Cite the turns or records it came from; a claim you cannot cite is not ready. What you propose waits for the owner's review — do not tell the user it is saved.

runner.guard: RunnerAuthGuard, plus the calling session (X-Orbit-Session-Id) checked the way runner-watches.controller.ts checks it
runner.maintenanceNote: phase 2; any other session is refused WIKI_NOT_MAINTENANCE_SESSION. The maintenance job's check (maintenance.job.check) also answers the space's owner's runner with no session, since a task's acceptance command runs with none.
runner.verificationNote: The session that proposed the ops, and no other (reviewModes.verification.who.runner): X-Orbit-Session-Id is required, and another session's op or another owner's anything is a 404.
runner.importNote: phase 2 (import): orbit wiki import's two routes, for a session of the space's owner — X-Orbit-Session-Id is required, and another owner's space is a 404.

verify.tool: none: a CLI verb with no MCP tool beside it. It runs a model, which is a runner's work rather than a tool call's, and it reports only what that model said.
verify.precondition: Verify only the ops this session proposed into an automatic space, and never write a verdict yourself: each verdict is the local model's, read from a separate clean call against the op's own sources, and a verdict that cannot be read is reported as nothing.
verify.does: Reads reviewModes.verification.list for --space, asks a clean Claude Code for one verdict per op, and reports each (reviewModes.verification.report) as soon as it has it, so what one run verified survives a run that stops half way. An op whose sources the list says are unreadable is asked about all the same: the server caps what its verdict can do (reviewModes.verification.evidence), and a duplicate still adds its sources. It stops at once on a 401 from the model's endpoint, and on a space that is no longer automatic.
verify.cleanClaudeCode: claude -p --bare --tools "" --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}' --no-session-persistence --output-format json --model <model> --system-prompt <the verifier's own, short> --settings <file naming an apiKeyHelper>, run with an empty HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and an environment built from an allowlist: none of the session's ORBIT_* variables, none of its own Claude Code's (of CLAUDE_CODE_* only the provider's CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS passes), and no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
verify.thinking: Off unless asked for: the clean call runs with CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL=unset and MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0, so its request names no effort and no thinking, whatever effort the session's provider declares. --effort <low|medium|high|xhigh|max> asks for that effort instead (CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL=<level>), and for thinking with it.
verify.model: The model and the endpoint are the ones the session's provider injected: ANTHROPIC_MODEL and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (--model names another model). The token is ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, read by the apiKeyHelper, because a bare run sends ANTHROPIC_API_KEY as x-api-key, which the local vLLM refuses 401, and ignores ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN.
verify.prompt: Hand-written, one op at a time: the entry's kind, title, summary and fields, the text of each source, and the neighbours a duplicate may name. The answer is one JSON object: {"verdict": one of reviewModes.verification.verdicts, "reason": one sentence, "duplicateOf": the id of the neighbour it duplicates, for a duplicate}.
verify.unreadable: An answer that is not that object — no JSON, another verdict, no reason, a duplicate naming no listed neighbour — is not a verdict: nothing is reported for its op, which keeps waiting, and it counts as a failure. The command exits non-zero when any op failed.

decide.sessionHeader: refused WIKI_OWNER_CHANNEL_ONLY whatever the session's role (the precedent is refuseSessionAuthoredConfirmation in coordinator-authority.ts)
decide.why: The confirmation card in the runner is not a gate: the server never checks it and a headless call passes it. So only the owner channel decides.

agentSurface.readBoundary: A session reads a space's entries only when its workspace is bound to that space: binding a workspace is the owner agreeing to share confirmed entries across the space's workspaces. A pending proposal is visible only to the session that made it.
agentSurface.excludedSessions: Verifier, foreman and judgment sessions are refused every wiki_* call (WIKI_SESSION_EXCLUDED) and are never pushed to.

rollout.canary: only the accounts ORBIT_WIKI_CANARY_OWNERS lists (comma-separated ids) have the wiki; every other account is as under off
rollout.off: the apiserver answers 404 WIKI_DISABLED on every route of both doors, the claim carries wikiDisabled, the runner mounts none of the three tools, no <orbit_wiki_context> is pushed, and an orbit-wiki: link card reads as unavailable

agentSurface.doorMissing: A runner newer than its apiserver says in a sentence that the server has no wiki door yet, as watch_tools.go's watchDoorMissing does.

realtime.scope: the space's owner, on the user-scoped control-plane stream (GET /api/events). The envelope names no session.
realtime.id: the space whose entries, review queue, bindings, settings, articles or plan changed
realtime.redaction: The space's id and nothing else: no entry, title, status, op or count. A client re-reads what it shows, and that read decides what it may see.
publishedWhen: a changeset recorded something, after its transaction commits
the owner decided ops, after the transaction commits
a space was created, its settings changed, or a workspace was bound
the owner reverted a changeset or rejected an entry, after the transaction commits
a verdict was recorded, after its transaction commits
pending ops expired or were withdrawn
a topic's articles were written, or a space's topics seeded, after the transaction commits
a version of a space's plan was stored or confirmed, or a change to it proposed or decided, after the transaction commits
a document's sections were written, after the transaction commits
realtime.correctness: Nothing depends on it. Dropping every announcement changes only how long a client waits: clients re-read on focus and on reconnect.
realtime.clientGroup: The web maps it to the wiki query group, never to groupsFor's default sessions group; Swift decodes it as ControlEvent.wikiChanged.

draft.summary: Deleting a record deletes every quote the wiki took from it.

fields.statement: When a record is deleted, every quote taken from it is deleted with it.
fields.rationale: Owners delete to forget; a wiki that kept the words would undo that.

vectors.why: The owner's new principle of 2026-09-25, spelled the way the owner writes one.

draft.title: Closed sets are CHECK constraints
draft.summary: A column with a closed set of values is TEXT with a CHECK, never an enum type.

fields.rule: Model a closed set as TEXT plus a CHECK constraint that lists its values.

vectors.why: exceptions is optional, and topics and aliases are optional common fields.

draft.title: Knowledge is stored as entries, not pages
draft.summary: The wiki stores atomic entries; pages, the decision log and the agent slice are views of them.

fields.context: People ask what is true now; agents need pitfalls and conventions.
fields.decision: Store atomic entries with sources and anchors, and project every page from them.

alternatives.whyRejected: Whole-page rewrites collapse, and a page cannot be reviewed item by item.

fields.consequences: Every view can be rebuilt; review and measurement are per entry.

vectors.why: A decision carries what was rejected and why; anchors of two types.

draft.title: A pg spec with no database skips and exits 0
draft.summary: node --test on a *.pg.spec with no COORDINATOR_PG_URL skips every case and still exits 0.

fields.symptom: A green acceptance run that witnessed no assertion.
fields.cause: Each pg spec skips itself when COORDINATOR_PG_URL is unset.
fields.fix: Run pg specs through scripts/run-pg-spec.sh, which provisions PostgreSQL and counts a skip as red.
fields.detector: grep '# skipped [1-9]' in the TAP summary

vectors.why: Every trigger key present; detector is optional.

draft.title: Run one pg spec against a throwaway PostgreSQL
draft.summary: scripts/run-pg-spec.sh builds the test tree, migrates a template and runs the spec on a clone.

steps: bash scripts/worktree-overlay.sh
bash scripts/run-pg-spec.sh src/apiserver/src/wiki/wiki-schema.pg.spec.ts

vectors.why: A recipe is steps plus the command that proves it worked.

draft.title: Space
draft.summary: One owner's wiki for one codebase.

fields.definition: A space is one owner's knowledge about one codebase, identified by its normalized repository URL.
fields.boundaries: A space never spans owners; workspaces bound to it share its confirmed entries.
fields.notToConfuseWith: A project, which is a goal and its tasks; several projects can share one space.
